lead_headline: 138 active restaurant leads tracked — 74 openings, 64 closures — with new spots in Rosedale, CBD, and Montbello emerging this week

restaurant.blurb: 3 new leads today: Noble Steakhouse (Union Station), Ariel's Cafe (Montbello), The Pearl lesbian bar closure (Five Points). Active: 138 leads total.

liquor.blurb: Zero new applications today, freezing the 7-day total at 2,386 licenses — up 39,667% from last week's 6 filings — as the database anomaly enters its third consecutive day of silence. Saturday's zero extends Friday's quiet, confirming the mass-filing event has fully exhausted itself after flooding the system mid-week. The 2,386-count spike represents batch renewals or backend processing, not organic business activity. Expect next week's rolling 7-day window to begin shedding this surge as the April flood exits the count, with weekly volumes forecast to revert to historical 20-30 baselines once the anomaly clears completely.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday holds the 7-day count at 44 across 13 sources — down 15% from last week's 52 mentions and extending the slowdown that began mid-April. Instagram dominates with 16 pickups (36% of weekly total), followed by Denver Post (6), Facebook (5), X (4), and Reddit (3). Saturday's single mention — an Instagram post about a Centennial multifamily development — mirrors Friday's lone pickup and confirms the weekend editorial lull. The 44-mention pace runs 7% above April's 41-weekly average, but back-to-back single-mention days signal May's opening momentum has stalled, with traditional news outlets continuing their post-April scale-back while social channels sustain baseline chatter.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +2 yesterday (2 new, 0 canceled) pushes MTD to +5 (+2.5/day), with 90-day net at +123. Friday's modest gain marks the third consecutive positive day, accumulating +9 across May 1-3 and stabilizing after the April 28th cancellation shock (17 cancellations). But the past week's −1 net (19 new, 20 canceled) continues eroding May's opening momentum — down sharply from last week's +15 — as persistent churn offsets new subscriber gains. MTD's +2.5/day rate runs 92% above YTD's +1.3/day baseline, suggesting May's opening burst is masking underlying volatility. The 14-day view shows recovery taking hold, but sustaining low-churn conversion remains critical to reclaim Q1's stability and validate May's pace.
